newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 4.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 4.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Wednesday:
** India on Tuesday outlined the steps the country needed to take to be able to float the rupee as a fully convertible currency by 2000.

A committee appointed by the RBI recommended targets for inflation and the country's fiscal deficit, deregulation of the interest rate structure and freedom for Indians to invest abroad as prerequisites for convertibility.
The rupee is currently convertible for current account, but not capital, transactions.

The committee, headed by former RBI deputy governor S.S. Tarapore, recommended a phased implementation of capital account convertibility over three years, and said the authorities should remain flexible in their approach.

** Indian Prime Minister I. K. Gujral said on Tuesday that a final decision on an increase in oil product prices would be taken on June 15 by the ruling United Front's steering committee, the Press Trust of India (PTI) reported.

"The issue of increase in prices of petroleum products will be decided finally at the steering committee meeting on June 15," PTI quoted Gujral as telling reporters after the induction of four ministers into his cabinet.

Strong opposition from left-wing constituents of the United Front had prevented the steering committee from arriving at a consensus on raising the prices of oil products at its last meeting on May 25.

** India's state-controlled power generation equipment maker Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd (BHEL) said on Wednesday that foreign institutional investors (FIIs) had increased their holding in the company to 16 percent.

"The foreign institutional holding has gone up to 16 percent in the company. The shares have not come for transfer, so I cannot say whether the FIIs are U.S. pension funds or not," BHEL's finance director K.G. Ramachandran told Reuters.
** Two-wheeler maker LML Ltd announced a six-month net profit of 172.0 million rupees in the period ending March 31, 1997 against a six-month comparision figure of 81.6 million rupees.
** Indian blue chips ended modestly higher on Tuesday, on the back of fund buying but a bout of profit-booking wiped gains made in a sharp rally, traders said.
** Bombay's benchmark 30-share index .BSESN ended 30.67 points, or 0.81 percent up at 3,838.85.
